title: In re Amendments to Florida Rule of General Practice and Judicial Administration 2.515
court: Supreme Court of Florida
sanctions_language: "sanctions may include reprimand, contempt, striking of the document, dismissal of proceedings, costs, attorneys’ fees, or other sanctions"
key_provisions: Rule 2.515(d)(2) was amended to require each signer to represent that legal authorities exist and are accurately cited.
The opinion identifies generative AI tools as drafting or research aids that can fabricate or hallucinate authorities.
The amendment applies to filings prepared by attorneys and by unrepresented parties.
The court may impose sanctions after notice and an opportunity to be heard.
Court commentary says the amendment replaces varied circuit AI disclosure and certification orders statewide.
summary: The Supreme Court of Florida amended Rule 2.515(d)(2), effective June 15, 2026, for all Florida court filings. Each signer represents that legal authorities exist and are accurately cited, and courts may sanction inconsistent filings after notice and an opportunity to be heard.
text_excerpt: "the legal authorities identified exist and are accurately cited"
notes: Opinion states the rule was adopted principally as a statewide, uniform replacement for varied circuit court AI disclosure and certification orders.

title: In re Amendments to Rules Regulating The Florida Bar – Chapter 4
court: Supreme Court of Florida
key_provisions: The opinion amends comments to Rules 4-1.1, 4-1.6, 4-5.1, and 4-5.3 to address generative AI.
Competence includes understanding benefits and risks of technology, including generative AI.
The confidentiality comment warns that generative AI may create risks to client confidentiality.
Supervisory comments direct lawyers to consider safeguards for generative AI use by lawyers and assistants.
summary: The Supreme Court of Florida amended comments to several Rules Regulating The Florida Bar, effective October 28, 2024. The AI provisions warn lawyers about competence, confidentiality, supervisory safeguards, and nonlawyer use of generative AI without creating a court-filing disclosure or certification requirement.
text_excerpt: "a lawyer should be aware that generative artificial intelligence may create risks to the lawyer’s duty of confidentiality"
notes: The AI language is in professional-conduct comments, not a filing-specific certification order.

title: Administrative Order No. 26-03: Prohibition on Use of Non-Approved Generative Artificial Intelligence Platforms by Court Personnel
court: Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida
sanctions_language: "Violations of this Administrative Order may result in corrective or disciplinary action"
key_provisions: Court personnel may not access, use, or input information into non-approved generative AI platforms for court business.
Non-approved platforms include public OpenAI tools, consumer web AI platforms, and tools lacking court-level privacy assurances.
Approved tools include court-authorized enterprise tools such as Microsoft Copilot and Westlaw AI-Assisted Research.
Approved tools must be accessed through authorized court systems and used under court technology and security policies.
summary: The Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida prohibits court personnel from using non-approved generative AI platforms for court business, effective January 15, 2026. Approved enterprise tools may be used through authorized court systems if users follow technology and security policies and remain responsible for work product.
text_excerpt: "Court Personnel shall not access, use, or input any information into Non-Approved Generative Artificial Intelligence Platforms"

title: Administrative Order No. 26-15: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Court Filings by Attorneys and Self-Represented Litigants
court: Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida
sanctions_language: "may result in sanctions, including but not limited to: the striking the filing"
key_provisions: AI may assist preparation, research, drafting, document review, filing review, discovery review, and discovery requests.
Use of generative AI to draft or generate content used in a filing or record must be disclosed.
The certification states the filer has read and verified citations, record citations, drafted language, quotations, facts, and legal analysis.
Disclosure is not required for routine research, cite-checking, or grammar, spelling, and clarity edits.
The order vacates and supersedes Administrative Order No. 26-04.
summary: The Eleventh Judicial Circuit of Florida requires attorneys and self-represented litigants to disclose generative AI use when it drafts or generates content used in court filings or records. Effective May 19, 2026, the required certification covers citations, record citations, drafted language, facts, and legal analysis.
text_excerpt: "The undersigned certifies that s/he has read and verified the accuracy of every citation to the law and/or the record"
notes: Order states it vacates and supersedes Administrative Order No. 26-04.
